lines.say: This painting is called The Nightmare. Henry Fuseli, 1781.
shots: archive: Fuseli The Nightmare 1781 (public domain), full

lines.say: A woman lies asleep, twisted across the bed. On her chest sits a demon, staring straight at us.
For centuries people described exactly this. Waking up, unable to move, with something heavy sitting on your chest, and a presence in the room.
In Newfoundland they called it the Old Hag. In other places, a witch, a jinn, a spirit.
Science calls it sleep paralysis. Your brain wakes up while your body is still locked in dream sleep, and the dream bleeds into the room.
shots: line art: brain awake, body asleep

lines.say: Studies suggest something like one person in twelve has it at least once.
So that demon on her chest? People really saw it. It just came from inside their own heads.
